name: Rome
tagline: Eternal City Living with La Dolce Vita on Any Budget
description: Rome offers a rare combination of world-class history, culture, and cuisine at prices that undercut most Western European capitals. The city rewards slow living — long espresso breaks, evening passeggiata, and neighborhood trattorias where a full meal costs less than a London appetizer. While bureaucracy and language barriers can be frustrating, Rome's quality of life and central Mediterranean location make it a compelling FIRE destination for those willing to embrace Italian rhythms.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day Schengen visa-free for US citizens; Elective Residency Visa for long-term stays
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – petty theft in tourist areas; otherwise safe
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with hot dry summers and mild wet winters

housing.description: Room in a shared flat / micro-studio in an outer/working district — Pigneto, Centocelle, Torpignattara, Quadraro

dining.description: Mostly home cooking from Roman markets, pizza al taglio and a trattoria lunch a few times a week

transportation.description: ATAC Metrebus personal monthly pass across metro/bus/tram

entertainment.description: Passeggiata, piazza life, first-Sunday museums and the Appian Way parks

1M.lifestyle: A room in a shared flat or a micro-studio in an outer, working district such as Pigneto, Centocelle, or Quadraro. Most meals are cooked at home from neighborhood-market produce, with pizza al taglio and a trattoria lunch a few times a week as the treat. Getting around runs on the ATAC monthly pass across metro, bus, and tram, and an ERV-compliant private health policy is carried from day one. Rome's free pleasures — the passeggiata, piazza life, first-Sunday museums, the parks along the Appian Way — carry the social calendar. It is a frugal but genuinely Roman rhythm where dining out and travel are planned rather than casual.

housing.description: Own studio/small 1BR (monolocale/bilocale), Garbatella / Ostiense / San Giovanni

dining.description: Neighborhood trattorias and osterias several nights a week with regular aperitivo

healthcare.description: Broad domestic private plan — good hospital network, specialist + dental

transportation.description: ATAC Metrebus personal monthly pass across metro/bus/tram

entertainment.description: Opera and museum memberships, cooking classes and weekend escapes

2M.lifestyle: A studio or small one-bedroom in a solid residential area like Garbatella, Ostiense, or San Giovanni. Dining out several times a week at neighborhood trattorias and osterias, with regular aperitivo and comprehensive private cover. Car-sharing or the train handles day trips, and weekends fold in escapes to the coast or the Castelli Romani. Everyday life is comfortable, food-rich, and rarely constrained by the bill.

housing.description: 1BR in a desirable central district — Trastevere, Monti, Prati, Testaccio

dining.description: Regular meals at well-regarded restaurants plus the daily espresso-bar ritual

healthcare.description: Broad-network private plan, wider hospital access (Gemelli, Villa Stuart), faster diagnostics

entertainment.description: Season opera tickets, gallery openings and frequent high-speed-rail getaways

3M.lifestyle: A one-bedroom in a desirable central district — Trastevere, Monti, Prati, or Testaccio — steps from the city's best cafés and markets. Regular dining at well-regarded restaurants, a broad-network private plan with fast specialist access at clinics like Gemelli or Villa Stuart, and a leased Vespa or small car for getting around. High-speed rail makes frequent weekends in Florence, Naples, or on the coast routine. This is a genuinely affluent Roman daily life with real room to travel.

housing.description: High-spec prime-central 1BR ~70 m², Centro Storico / Prati / Aventino

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the city's top tables and enoteca evenings

healthcare.description: Premium / entry-level international plan, regional/EU cover, direct billing

transportation.description: Luxury car + parking garage + first-class Trenitalia

entertainment.description: Private museum tours, exclusive cultural events and Tyrrhenian boating

5M.lifestyle: A high-spec prime-central one-bedroom in the Centro Storico, Prati, or Aventino, near the Pantheon and Navona. Near-daily dining at the city's top tables, premium private health cover, regular housekeeping, and a luxury car with a parking garage. First-class Trenitalia and frequent European travel are routine, and weekends drift to Umbrian hill towns. Rome's moderate underlying costs mean this tier delivers an upper-affluent life with generous slack for culture and travel.

housing.description: Luxury 1–2BR ~95–110 m² at a prime address, Centro Storico / Parioli / Prati

dining.description: Private-chef-level dining and Rome's finest restaurants, hosted dinners

healthcare.description: Top-tier worldwide cover (Cigna Global / Bupa Global, incl. evacuation)

transportation.description: Chauffeured car on top of transit + private transfers

entertainment.description: Art patronage, private Vatican tours and Mediterranean yacht charters

luxuryExtras.description: Private-jet access, vineyard interest, art acquisitions, foundation

10M.lifestyle: A luxury one-to-two-bedroom at a landmark address — a palazzo apartment overlooking a piazza, or a place in leafy Parioli. Private-chef-level dining and the finest restaurants in the city, top-tier international health cover with global evacuation, a chauffeured car layered on transit, and full household help. Travel is first-class by default and the discretionary budget stretches to art, a vineyard interest, and a second base in Tuscany or on the coast. At this level Rome is comfortably within reach with margin to spare.
